speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been progressing, and have you noticed any specific changes in your vision or coordination?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Prion disease (likely sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease).

The combination of rapidly progressive dementia (6 months), myoclonus-like agitation, and acute cerebellar signs (falls, gait ataxia, leg weakness) in a 44-year-old is highly suggestive. REQUEST TEST: CSF_14-3-3 and CSF_Tau; REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI.
